title: Add audit log pipeline lag metric + alert thresholds (enterprise-aligned) and update runbook
creator: Allison Grant
project: CS & Support Escalation Playbook Refresh / Known-Issues Sprint (Feb 2026)
description:
Context
- Support/CS escalations (notably SUP-1846 / Vertex LegalTech) indicate we lack a single, Support-verifiable signal for “audit logs are behind”. Today triage relies on ad-hoc queries and engineer-only dashboards.
- Enterprise expectations: audit logs are operationally sensitive (compliance workflows). When delayed, customers need fast confirmation + clear comms.

Goal
- Add a first-class metric representing audit log delivery lag and wire it to:
  1) a Support-safe dashboard panel (by region + sink type)
  2) alert thresholds aligned to enterprise expectations (warning + paging)
  3) an updated runbook that Support can follow (what to check, what to say, when to escalate)

Non-goals
- Re-architect the audit log pipeline.
- Add per-customer alerting (too high-cardinality). We will instead provide region/sink level signals + an internal query recipe for specific tenant confirmation.

Proposed metric (definition + naming)
- Metric name (internal standard): redwood_auditlog_delivery_lag_seconds
- Type: gauge (reported continuously)
- Dimensions/labels:
  - region (us-east, us-west, eu-west, ap-southeast)
  - sink_type (s3_export, webhook_delivery, console_view)
  - tier_bucket (enterprise, non_enterprise)  [derived from routing/tenant metadata, aggregated]
- Definition:
  - “Delivery lag” = now() - max(delivered_event_time) over a rolling window of delivered audit log events, per region/sink.
  - Implementation detail: for sinks that are push-based (webhook), use acknowledged delivery timestamp. For batch exports (S3), use batch watermark time. For console view, use indexing watermark.
- Rationale:
  - Using watermark-based lag avoids per-tenant labels while still surfacing the user-visible symptom: newest available audit log entry is stale.

Alerting (enterprise-aligned thresholds)
- Alert targets: SRE on-call (page on critical), #eng-sre (warn), and a non-paging notification to #support-oncall (for awareness + faster customer comms).

Suggested thresholds (initial)
- Warning (ticketable / investigate):
  - Condition: lag > 10 minutes for 15 minutes (per region + sink)
  - Severity: Sev3 (internal), do not page; send Slack + create incident note in SRE channel.
  - Rationale: catches emerging backlog before enterprise customers hit the 30+ minute mark.
- Critical (page):
  - Condition: lag > 30 minutes for 10 minutes (enterprise bucket) OR lag > 45 minutes for 10 minutes (non-enterprise bucket)
  - Severity: Sev2 (internal) page SRE on-call.
  - Rationale: matches recurring enterprise pain point from SUP-1846 and comms commitments (customers perceive 30+ min as “broken”).

Notes
- We expect some sinks (S3 export) to show step-function behavior (batching). For S3, use a sink-specific “expected batch interval” annotation in dashboard and tune warning threshold to avoid constant noise.
- Add inhibition logic: if region-wide control plane incident is active, suppress duplicate pages and attach to the parent incident.

Dashboard updates
- Add a panel to the “Audit Logs - Health” dashboard:
  - redwood_auditlog_delivery_lag_seconds by region, split by sink_type
  - Overlay alert thresholds (10m / 30m)
  - Add a short text panel: “How to interpret this metric” + link to runbook
- Add a Support-safe “quick view” (read-only) that does not expose tenant identifiers.

Runbook updates (Support + SRE)
- Update the audit log delivery runbook to include:
  - Confirming customer symptoms:
    - “Newest audit log event timestamp in Console / export destination”
    - region + sink type + approximate delay
  - Support-side checks (no privileged access):
    - Verify if lag dashboard indicates region-wide delay
    - Verify if there’s an active status page incident or internal #incidents thread
  - SRE checks (privileged):
    - consumer lag by topic, error rates, webhook delivery retries, export job backlog
  - Mitigations checklist:
    - Scale consumers/workers
    - Pause non-essential backfills
    - Increase webhook concurrency / adjust retry backoff temporarily
    - For S3: force a manual export job kick if backlog is stuck (if safe)
  - Customer comms guidance:
    - Clarify scope (region-wide vs account-specific)
    - Set expectation: “We are delivering with delay; data is not lost; we will provide next update at <cadence>”
    - Explicitly avoid promising exact catch-up time until backlog drain rate is confirmed
  - Escalation triggers:
    - Any enterprise customer reporting > 15 min perceived lag OR lag panel > 30 min
    - Compliance deadlines mentioned (audit/export needed for filing)

Rollout plan
1) Ship metrics + dashboard panel to staging; validate values with synthetic audit events.
2) Shadow alerting for 48 hours (Slack-only) to tune sink-specific noise (especially S3).
3) Enable paging for enterprise-bucket critical threshold.
4) Publish updated runbook + link it from Support Known Issue article and Support macros.

Acceptance criteria
- Dashboard shows a reasonable lag value in each region for at least 2 sink types (webhook + S3), updated at least every 1 minute.
- Warning and critical alerts fire in a controlled test (synthetic lag injection / paused consumer in staging).
- On-call runbook includes:
  - where to look
  - how to validate impact
  - mitigation playbook
  - comms pointers for Support
- Support can answer within 5 minutes: “Is audit log lag a platform issue right now? Which regions/sinks are affected?”

Open questions / follow-ups
- Do we want the enterprise bucket to be strictly contract-tier, or “any tenant with audit log add-on”? (Default: contract-tier enterprise for now.)
- Long-term: add a tenant-scoped query snippet (internal only) that Support can request from SRE to confirm account-specific delays without broad data access.

Implementation
- Implemented in observability-pack (see PR-711) with dashboard + alerts + runbook links.
- Coordinated with Support/CS to ensure terminology matches KB article and SLA update cadence language.
